problem: Crouzeix's conjecture: the matrix norm of a complex function f applied to a complex matrix A is at most twice the supremum of |f(z)| over the field of values of A.
missing_details: The norm on the left-hand side is the spectral operator 2-norm
The function f must be analytic on the interior of W(A) and continuous on its closure
The field of values W(A) is defined as {x*Ax: x∈C^n, ||x||=1}
A is required to be an n×n complex square matrix
The definition of f(A) relies on the holomorphic functional calculus
refined_question: Let A be an n×n complex matrix and let W(A)={x*Ax: x∈C^n, ||x||=1} denote its field of values. Let f be a function analytic on an open set containing W(A) and continuous on its closure, and let ||·|| denote the spectral operator 2-norm on C^n. Does the inequality ||f(A)|| ≤ 2 sup_{z∈W(A)}|f(z)| hold for every such A and f?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every n×n complex matrix A and every complex polynomial p, does ||p(A)|| ≤ 2 sup_{z∈W(A)}|p(z)| hold, where ||·|| is the spectral operator 2-norm?
justification: The name captures the core inequality and objects (matrix norm, function f, field of values, factor 2) but omits norms specification, analytic conditions on f, precise definition of W(A), matrix dimensions, and the polynomial-only variant. The completeness score reflects these omissions.
